items.title: School/Community Reports – Recommended Options to the School Board Regarding North Star Academy (NSA)

publicComments.name: Matt Schwal
publicComments.summary: Argued the NSA Forward Committee was negatively framed and called on board members to reframe the discussion positively and inspire change rather than break what is working.

publicComments.name: Cameron Hoffman
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposals are rushed and lack an evidence-based approach, and proposed a 'SHINE' talent development program modeled on the U46 district's AIM program to serve all neighborhood school students rather than restructuring North Star.

publicComments.name: Tony Webel
publicComments.summary: Shared his experience as both a Roosevelt and North Star parent, argued there is no data justifying grade configuration or location changes, and cited board bylaws requiring decisions be based on student learning and achievement.

publicComments.name: Diana Fu
publicComments.summary: Drew on her experience helping start the MI program to argue the district should provide more and better school choices rather than taking away the North Star option from parents.

publicComments.name: Lone Hin
publicComments.summary: Described her son's unmet needs at his neighborhood school and argued that dismantling or scaling back North Star would not serve any children in the district.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Neill
publicComments.summary: Argued that options A through C would eliminate half of North Star and fail to meet the stated goal of serving more students more effectively, and that no changes should happen until neighborhood schools can serve the needs of academically challenged students.

publicComments.name: Matt Collier
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to choose an option that allows K–8 programming to continue as a standalone school, sharing his personal experience benefiting from similar magnet programs.

publicComments.name: Anthony Low
publicComments.summary: As a Roy Cloud and North Star parent, argued all four options are deficient, that three of them effectively close 50% of North Star, and that his family would likely have to leave the district if a 6–8 option were chosen.

publicComments.name: Andrew Hoffman
publicComments.summary: Argued the board should focus on lifting lower-performing parts of the district rather than negatively impacting the award-winning North Star, and urged the board not to hastily approve incomplete recommendations.

publicComments.name: Heidi Wall
publicComments.summary: Argued the district should focus on systemic problems rather than dismantling a successful school, and cited the U46 model as a proven approach to improving diversity without restructuring.

publicComments.name: Susan Bouchard
publicComments.summary: Opposed the quota cap on neighborhood school transfers to NSA, arguing it would increase perceptions of elitism and division, and asked why the cap is not applied to all school-of-choice programs.

publicComments.name: Costas Dimitropoulos
publicComments.summary: Called for empirical evidence and proven models to justify any changes to North Star, noting that demographic differences between schools reflect local demographics rather than the influence of North Star.

publicComments.name: Kelly McCarthy
publicComments.summary: Questioned why the district is prioritizing North Star changes when so many students are underperforming post-COVID, and urged the board to use those resources to bolster neighborhood school programs instead.

publicComments.name: Casey Wright
publicComments.summary: Called the four options deeply flawed and irresponsible without fuller analysis of consequences, urged the board to postpone consideration and demand new options like those proposed by Cameron Hoffman.

publicComments.name: Catherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Noted that all speakers before her opposed changes to North Star, and argued that the 'rising tide lifts all boats' principle means the school should be kept as-is rather than changed to reduce resentment from other schools.

publicComments.name: Gautam Dutta
publicComments.summary: As a North Star parent and community leader, echoed the sentiment that North Star is working well for his daughter and urged the board to reject all four options and instead focus on improving access and resources for all schools.

publicComments.name: Jing Su
publicComments.summary: Warned that the proposed changes would create many unhappy parents who would become reliable voters opposing the board, and urged trustees to consider the daily disruption to North Star families before making their decision.

publicComments.name: Kirsten McMullen
publicComments.summary: Argued the recommendations lack an evidence-based approach, only adequately solve the third-grade attrition problem while creating new unknowns, and urged additional research before selecting any option.

publicComments.name: Bara Altaba
publicComments.summary: As a parent of current NSA students who came from private school because of NSA, urged the board not to break a nationally recognized school and instead look at how to bring other schools up to NSA's level.

publicComments.name: Michelle Fogarty
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposals take direct aim at one successful school rather than addressing full district needs, and urged the board to take more time, examine the data framework, and conduct a new community survey before acting.

publicComments.name: Katie Goetz
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member, encouraged the board to move forward with the 6–8 Bayside option as the one proposal that addresses all three charges given to the committee.

publicComments.name: Christopher Bouchard
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to reject all four proposals and pause major changes, arguing the NSA Forward process was flawed from the beginning due to outdated and biased data, and called for a new community pulse survey.

publicComments.name: David Wright
publicComments.summary: Implored the board to defer the decision and request revised options informed by data that directly align to the committee's stated goals, rather than committing to deeply flawed options.

publicComments.name: Mike Beebe
publicComments.summary: Identified three broadly supported elements from Dr. Baker's plans (publicizing NSA, test prep/logistics help, and transportation), suggested spreading entrance grades across 3rd–5th to blunt the third-grade attrition pinch, and argued the board's primary focus should be the 52–72% of district students not at grade level.

publicComments.name: Meredith Park
publicComments.summary: As a Sequoia High parent and safe-routes advocate, warned that adding K–2 at the Duane location would worsen traffic, and suggested considering a neighborhood boundary middle school with an IB program at that site instead.

publicComments.name: Nathan Schmidt
publicComments.summary: Used a boat analogy to argue the board must focus on lifting underperforming schools rather than 'dumping water' into the one that is floating, urging them not to take action merely to appear as change agents.

publicComments.name: Mohamed Tabrizi
publicComments.summary: Ceded his time to Cameron Hoffman, agreed with her sentiments, and called the entire process a waste of resources that should have gone toward educating lower-income students, urging trustees to reject all options.

publicComments.name: Lily Melton
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent, urged the board to move forward with bold structural changes, noting that a large community of district parents supports significant changes even if they are not the loudest voices tonight.

publicComments.name: Beatrice Chan
publicComments.summary: As a North Star parent, asked the board to present new options focused on introducing enrichment programs at community schools and helping current students meet grade-level expectations, rather than dismantling a successful model.

publicComments.name: Maribel Ng
publicComments.summary: Shared her daughter's struggles before finding North Star and argued that spreading the North Star philosophy of seeing students as individuals and loving what you teach across all Redwood City schools would fix many district-wide problems.
